critique_dispositions.reason: Retry count is additional retries, so three permits four attempts.
Per-transfer counter resets; retry-max-time does not stop a transfer already in progress. A product supervisor deadline addresses the separate process bound.
Original O5 is the governing primary product obligation. Library-document silence cannot remove cancellation. No invented curl requirement is needed.
Mutating endpoints violate O3 and retry_scope=read_only_get; all-error retry duplicates are documented.
Default received HTTP error pages need explicit failure handling. The chosen fail-with-body is available and preserves the body. Final line 9 adds the separate incorrect retry-extension claim F2.
Retry-After support since 7.66.0 is in the 8.10.1 source. Correct preservation of support does not verify unconditional delay override F1.

material_findings.title: Retry-After is incorrectly described as overriding the computed delay

candidate_locator.exact_text: The server's `Retry-After:` response header, honored since curl 7.66.0 and present in 8.10.1, overrides the computed delay for the next retry.

related_candidate_locators.exact_text: `Retry-After` override behavior against a stub server
--retry-delay disables the algorithm; server Retry-After overrides per-attempt delay.

material_findings.supported_finding: In the target CLI implementation, a parsed positive Retry-After is used only for an already eligible transient HTTP retry, and changes the sleep only when its seconds converted to milliseconds exceed the existing computed sleep. It cannot shorten exponential backoff. When elapsed retry time plus Retry-After exceeds retry-max-time, the CLI exits the retry path instead of scheduling the promised next retry. The candidate describes unconditional override and carries it into the proposed timing evidence.
material_findings.materiality: This determines actual request scheduling and a prospective acceptance oracle, both expressly required by O3. A shorter header and a budget-exceeding header produce different behavior from the saved policy.
material_findings.static_counterexample: With a computed second-retry delay of 2 seconds and a valid Retry-After: 1, the source keeps 2 seconds. With --retry-max-time 45 and Retry-After: 60 on the first eligible HTTP error, the source takes the no-retry branch. These are source-derived examples, not executed runtime observations.
material_findings.bounded_supported_scope: Support since 7.66.0 is correct; critique 6 should remain rejected. The defect is the unsupported exact scheduling rule, not the existence of Retry-After support.

material_findings.axis: Factual applicability / O3 HTTP failure reporting versus retry eligibility
material_findings.title: The final claims that fail-with-body extends HTTP retry eligibility

candidate_locator.exact_text: Combined with `--retry`, failure semantics extend retries to HTTP error statuses; without this option the draft's claim that every unsuccessful status already fails is wrong.

related_candidate_locators.exact_text: With --retry, some transient HTTP codes retry; most 4xx still do not. With --fail, HTTP error codes fail/retry.
Most 4xx statuses, such as 404, are not transient and are never retried by `--retry` alone.

material_findings.supported_finding: In curl 8.10.1, --fail-with-body converts a fully received HTTP 400+ response into exit error 22. It does not extend the transient HTTP retry set. Both successful-transfer results without a failure option and error-22 results with a failure option enter the same response-status switch, which allows only 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504. Retrying other error statuses requires the separate retry-all-errors fallback, which the candidate explicitly disables.
material_findings.materiality: This conflates status reporting with retry eligibility in the standalone policy. A normally received 404 is terminal with --retry 3 --fail-with-body, while a 503 is eligible for retry even without fail-with-body; the asserted extension is false under either reading.
material_findings.static_counterexample: A fully received 404 sets result to CURLE_HTTP_RETURNED_ERROR, matches no transient switch case, and is not retried when retry_all_errors is false. This is a static implementation trace, not a runtime test.
material_findings.bounded_supported_scope: Critique 5 is correctly accepted: explicit HTTP failure handling is necessary, and fail-with-body is a supported body-preserving choice. That correct correction does not support widening HTTP retry eligibility.

limitations.description: The candidate labels the newest in-page version string as 8.22.0, while the identical 465220-byte live page explicitly describes curl 8.23.0 in its Version section. Target behavioral claims were pinned to 8.10.1, so this provenance-label mistake is not a separate material policy defect.

The source map transfers fail.md's 401/407 authentication caveat to the chosen fail-with-body option without distinguishing implementations. The latter is handled in post_per_transfer after transfer completion. No authentication workflow is specified in this fixture, and no consequential authentication decision is made in the final; this is recorded as a source-map limitation, not another material finding.

The three required checks are meaningful but do not discriminate F1/F2. The persistent-500 exhaustion expectation needs a fast stub and bounded delays to fit the supervisor deadline. No actual implementation, deployment or additional mandatory test is demanded.

useful_discoveries.discovery: Version-exact transient HTTP set excludes modern 522/524 additions.
Retry-After predates 8.10.1; introduction availability is separate from later option semantics.
fail-with-body preserves an HTTP error body whereas fail suppresses it; both cannot be enabled together.
retry-delay is a fixed-delay alternative; leaving it unset preserves exponential backoff.
A process supervisor is the appropriate separate mechanism for the absolute product deadline.
useful_discoveries.kind: product inference from documented flag limits

useful_discoveries.discovery: Retry-After lengthens but cannot shorten the existing backoff and may terminate retries when its requested delay exceeds retry-max-time.
HTTP failure reporting and HTTP retry eligibility are distinct branches; --fail-with-body does not add status cases.

The implementation also retries host/proxy resolution errors, although the short retry manual lists timeouts and response codes. Connection-refused retry is a separate opt-in. This is an implementation lead, not a demand to expand the product policy or a third failure finding.
